name: The Dewberry Charleston
positioning: Mid-century modern hotel in a restored 1960s federal building on Marion Square in downtown Charleston, owned by John Dewberry
best_for: Design lovers who want mid-century modern style and artisan details
Travelers who want a downtown Charleston base with house-car rides, bicycles and concierge-arranged outings on the water

facts.text: The Dewberry borders Marion Square, a public park that hosts some of the city's most popular events.
The hotel occupies Charleston's L. Mendel Rivers Federal Building (circa 1964), a mid-century modern landmark rescued, restored and reimagined by owner John Dewberry.
The building was reimagined over eight years by a team of architects and designers.
Design details include hand-gilded cranes in the Swanston Room, custom botanical armoires, Vermont-selected marble, vintage Danish furnishings and a bespoke Woka brass chandelier.
Rooms have custom Stickley armoires with botanical patterns, baths of Vermont marble, mattresses imported from Ireland and chef-curated mini-bars.
The Charleston Flats sit in the corners of each floor.
The extraordinarily tall windows date to when JFK originally commissioned the building.
The Spa is softly lit, cypress lined and curtain draped, and offers Natura Bisse facials, hot river stone massages and detoxifying seaweed wraps.
Complimentary Volvo house car transportation is offered to select destinations in downtown Charleston, based on availability.
The hotel has a fleet of 21-gear Specialized bicycles with racks and baskets for cruising around the peninsula.
Hotel guests can book a privately guided introduction to The Charleston Library Society.
The Dewberry was named in Conde Nast Traveler's Readers' Choice Awards every year from 2017 to 2026.

highlights.text: The John Derian Flat blends Derian's signature decoupage pieces with vintage-inspired goods and textiles.
The Dewberry is the exclusive Charleston hotel partner of Barton & Gray, so guests can charter a classic Hinckley Talaria yacht to see Charleston and the barrier islands from the water.
One-Bedroom Suites have a separate bedroom with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking Historic Charleston and Marion Square.
Citrus Club occupies the hotel's eighth-floor terrace and is the highest rooftop lounge in Charleston, with 360-degree views over the peninsula.
The concierge can schedule a five-hour beach trip in a Volvo house car, packed with beach chairs, an umbrella, towels and cold waters.

considerations.text: Parking is valet only, at $58 per night; self-parking is not offered.
Pets are not permitted, though service animals are welcome, and rollaway beds are not available; cribs can be arranged through the Concierge.
Citrus Club, the rooftop lounge, is for guests 21 and older.
